{{Short description|Geometrical smooth strip}}
In [[differential geometry]], a '''ribbon''' (or '''strip''') is the combination of a [[smoothness|smooth]] [[space curve]] and its corresponding [[normal vector]]. More formally, a ribbon denoted by <math>(X,U)</math> includes a curve <math>X</math> given by a three-dimensional [[Vector (mathematics and physics)|vector]] <math>X(s)</math>, depending continuously on the curve [[Arc length|arc-length]] <math>s</math> (<math>a\leq s \leq b</math>), and a unit vector <math>U(s)</math> perpendicular to <math>{\partial X \over \partial s}(s)</math> at each point.<ref>Blaschke, W. (1950) ''Einführung in die Differentialgeometrie''. Springer-Verlag. {{isbn|9783817115495}}</ref> Ribbons have seen particular application as regards [[DNA]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Vologodskiǐ |first=Aleksandr Vadimovich |title=Topology and Physics of Circular DNA |year=1992 |isbn=<!--978-1-315-12130-7-->978-1138105058 |edition=First |location=Boca Raton, FL |page=49 |oclc=1014356603}}</ref>

==Properties and implications==
The ribbon <math>(X,U)</math> is called ''simple'' if <math>X</math> is a [[simple curve]] (i.e. without self-intersections) and ''closed'' and if <math>U</math> and all its derivatives agree at <math>a</math> and <math>b</math>. 
For any simple closed ribbon the curves <math>X+\varepsilon U</math> given parametrically by <math>X(s)+\varepsilon U(s)</math> are, for all sufficiently small positive <math>\varepsilon</math>, simple closed curves disjoint from <math>X</math>.

The ribbon concept plays an important role in the '''Călugăreanu formula''',<ref>{{cite journal|last=Fuller|first=F. Brock|title=The writhing number of a space curve|journal=[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America]]|year=1971|volume=68|issue=4|pages=815–819|doi=10.1073/pnas.68.4.815|mr=0278197|pmid=5279522|pmc=389050|bibcode=1971PNAS...68..815B|doi-access=free|url=http://www.pnas.org/content/68/4/815.full.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dennis |first1=M. R. |last2=Hannay |first2=J. H. |title=Geometry of Călugăreanu's theorem |journal=Proceedings of the Royal Society A |date=26 August 2005 |volume=461 |issue=2062 |pages=3245–3254 |doi=10.1098/rspa.2005.1527 |arxiv=math-ph/0503012 |bibcode=2005RSPSA.461.3245D |url=https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/rspa.2005.1527}}</ref> that states that

:<math>Lk = Wr + Tw ,</math>

where <math>Lk</math> is the asymptotic (Gauss) ''[[linking number]]'', the integer number of turns of the ribbon around its axis; <math>Wr</math> denotes the total ''writhing number'' (or simply ''[[writhe]]''), a measure of non-planarity of the ribbon's axis curve; and <math>Tw</math> is the total ''twist number'' (or simply ''[[Twist (differential geometry)|twist]]''), the rate of rotation of the ribbon around its axis.

Ribbon theory investigates geometric and topological aspects of a mathematical reference ribbon associated with physical and biological properties, such as those arising in [[topological fluid dynamics]], [[DNA]] modeling and in [[material science]].
